honesty: Colour, opacity, rise velocity, particle size and duration are artistic choices. The straight smoke column is a depiction of a cited claim (Avos 5:5), not a physical result. Nothing here is rabbinic approval.

sourceClaims.claim: The column of smoke from the arrangement was not dispersed by the wind.
sourceClaims.source: Avos 5:5 (among the miracles of the Mikdash)
sourceClaims.depiction: OuterAltarColumn is authored vertical at every wind speed. This is a depiction of a cited claim, not a physical result; the physical bent-plume path stays in PlumeMath.h and is separately tested.

sourceClaims.claim: A perpetual fire shall burn on the altar; it shall not go out.
sourceClaims.depiction: The outer altar fire is the only continuous effect in the set.

sourceClaims.claim: A stafflike column rose to the ceiling, and the smoke then spread and descended until the chamber was filled.
sourceClaims.depiction: Narrow indoor column (entrainment 0.06), ceiling impingement, radial ceiling jet, descending layer. Velocities, depths and durations are design values; the sugya gives none.

sourceClaims.claim: Incense twice daily on the Golden Altar in the Heikhal, tied to tending the lamps.
sourceClaims.depiction: The ketores plume is an event with a start and an end, driven by AMikdashServiceActor through AMikdashFXDirector, not a permanent emitter. Research dossier Research/ketores-service-and-smoke.md is explicit that 'regular service' is not evidence for a continuous emitter.

sourceClaims.claim: Beaten olive oil for the light, to kindle a lamp continually.
sourceClaims.depiction: Wick-scale flames, warm and small, one small light each. Not torch scale.

sourceClaims.claim: The texts give qualitative behaviour and no measured colour, opacity, rise velocity, particle size or persistence.
sourceClaims.depiction: Every colour, opacity, speed and duration in this manifest is labelled a design value and none is presented as measured.

materials.name: M_FX_Point

instances.name: MI_FX_Ember
instances.note: Log-normal burnout, median 1.60 s, 95th percentile 3.95 s.

instances.name: MI_FX_DustMote
instances.note: Soft and dim. A mote is an out-of-focus speck, and a hard sprite at this size aliases into sparkle.

instances.name: MI_FX_LightShaft
instances.note: Brightness falls as |dot(view, card normal)| raised to ViewFalloffPower, so the beam vanishes when you look along it instead of becoming a visible sheet.

instances.name: MI_FX_HeatHaze

rtx2070Estimate.translucentBasis: The director holds total translucent overdraw to 3 screen areas and lowers EffectsQuality when it does not. 3 x 1920 x 1080 is 6.2 Mpixel of translucent shading; these materials are two texture fetches and about 30 ALU each, which a 2070 covers comfortably inside 2 ms.
rtx2070Estimate.dynamicLightsBasis: Eight movable point lights, all shadowless: the altar fire plus one per lamp. The lamp lights reach 260 cm, so each covers a small screen footprint. A shadow-casting flickering fire light would cost more than this whole set and is deliberately not used.
rtx2070Estimate.realRisk: Draw calls, not fill. 295 cards is the arithmetic worst case; the altar group and the Heikhal group are 30 m apart and the per-anchor distance quality means both are never at full detail at once, so the practical range is 40 to 90 cards. That is CPU-side and is what to watch on a capture.
rtx2070Estimate.notMeasured: Nobody has run this on a 2070. These are budgets to check a capture against.

effects.label: Outer altar fire
effects.notes: Additive flame cards sitting on the wood arrangement, 325.0 cm across, flicker 0.83205 Hz.

effects.label: Outer altar smoke column
effects.notes: Vertical at every wind speed. Source claim, not physics.

effects.label: Outer altar embers
effects.notes: Log-normal burnout, median 1.6 s, 95th percentile 3.9538 s.

effects.label: Fire light on the surrounding stone
effects.notes: One movable point light, 2100 K, flickered by the same FFlicker stream as the flame cards so light and flame agree.

effects.label: Faint smoke haze near the altar
Ketores plume on the golden altar
effects.notes: Event, not an emitter. Rises then spreads. Reaches the ceiling in 43.799885 s.

effects.label: Ketores ceiling layer
effects.notes: Spreads to 1050.0 cm and descends to 949.9992 cm. Stops at the ceiling; it never leaves the roof.

effects.label: Menorah seven lamps
effects.notes: Wick 0.6 cm, flicker 19.364917 Hz, 7.0 cm tall, one 1.4 cd light each.

effects.label: Light shafts in the Heikhal
effects.notes: Card beams from the Heikhal doorway wall toward the floor. Design: the window arrangement is not settled, so the shaft anchors are spec data and marked needs_review.
effects.needsReview: Heikhal window positions are not settled in this build; the shaft origins are authored, not derived from a window mesh.

effects.label: Dust motes in the shafts
effects.notes: Motes drift only inside the shaft volumes; outside them they are invisible, which is what makes a shaft read as light.

effects.label: Heat shimmer over the fire and haze over the courts at midday
effects.notes: Refraction-only cards. The first sits directly over the fire and is the altar's own heat shimmer; it is always on, because a fire is hot at any hour. The rest are the court haze and are scaled by HeatHazeStrength, which the time-of-day system drives through AMikdashFXDirector::SetHeatHazeStrength so this actor never reads the clock itself.

limitations: The MenorahV4 model is the Temple Institute display vessel: each lamp bowl (local Z 142.17..143.94 cm) carries a decorative lid (143.745..146.67) and a finial (146.67..150). The model has no exposed wick. The flame is therefore authored at the lid crown, local Z 146.67, so that it reads as a lit lamp; lampFlameLocalZCm in the spec moves it back to the bowl rim if the menorah model is ever given open bowls. This is a modelling compromise, recorded, not a claim about the vessel.

Heat shimmer, the light shafts and the heat haze are camera-facing translucent cards with a refraction/panner treatment, not a volumetric or a screen-space distortion pass. They read correctly from the reviewed visitor viewpoints and will not survive an arbitrary flythrough.
The GPU numbers in this manifest are overdraw arithmetic, not a measured capture on an RTX 2070.
Nothing here is rabbinic approval, and no part of this depicts the incense formula, maaleh ashan's botanical identity, or a rule about service.
